title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
statement: Return the kth largest element in `nums`. It is the kth element in sorted order, not the kth distinct element.
hints: Sorting and indexing at n - k is correct and costs n log n.
A min-heap of size k keeps the k largest elements. The root is the kth largest.
Quickselect finds the element at index n - k in expected linear time by partitioning like quicksort and recurring into one side.

approaches.name: Sort
approaches.explanation: Return the element at index n - k after sorting ascending.

approaches.name: Heap of size k
approaches.explanation: Push every element and pop when the heap exceeds k.

approaches.name: Quickselect
approaches.explanation: Partition until the pivot lands on n - k.

editorial: The heap solution is the one to reach for when k is small and the stream might be online. Maintain a min-heap. After processing the array its size is k and its smallest element is the kth largest in the whole array. Quickselect is faster on average but has a quadratic worst case unless the pivot is chosen carefully.

examples.explanation: Duplicates count separately. The 4th largest is 4.
